ROLE: Bring a byte_buf into the canonical empty state (data NULL, len 0, cap 0) without touching any storage.

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: buffer that becomes the empty buffer

LOGIC.INPUT: buf, a caller-owned buffer object, or NULL.
LOGIC.ACTION: If buf is NULL return immediately. Otherwise set buf->data = NULL, buf->len = 0 and buf->cap = 0. No allocation, no free: any storage previously reachable from buf->data must already have been released by the caller (buffer_free), because init is used by owners on freshly created objects only.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: buf denotes an empty buffer with no owned storage; the function returns no value.
INVARIANTS_USED: a zero cap means no storage may be read or written
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: buf points to writable storage of sizeof(struct byte_buf) or is NULL; buf->data is not owned by any other live object.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe: the caller owns the buffer exclusively.
